An accent mark disappears from a name. A search misses the message it was
supposed to find. A model gives a fluent answer that is wrong. Language feels
effortless until a computer handles it badly.

Natural language processing, usually shortened to **NLP**, studies how
computers work with human language. The field contains dozens of connected
tasks. This table gives each one a place, a short name, and eventually a lesson
that shows why it matters.

::: {.callout-tip}
## New to R?

Start with task 1, then continue in number order. Later lessons explain their
main idea from the beginning, but their code can use R syntax introduced
earlier. Each lesson begins with a human problem and shows the output produced
by real code.
:::

## Explore the periodic table {#periodic-table-heading}

The table works like a memory map. A task's color shows its broad stage, while
its position places it beside related work. The short symbol makes the tile
easy to recognize when you return.

::: {.callout-note}
## What this map is

This is a teaching aid, not a scientific taxonomy or a complete account of the
field. It mixes tasks, methods, objectives, resources, services, applications,
and work done across a model's life. Each tile names its item type so those
differences remain visible. Some inherited group names are broad or imperfect;
the lesson attached to a tile must explain such limits.
:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

options(warn = 2)

task_map <- read.csv(
  "data/periodic_table.csv",
  colClasses = c(
    task_number = "integer",
    symbol = "character",
    title = "character",
    item_type = "character",
    group_id = "integer",
    group_name = "character",
    stage = "character",
    lesson_path = "character",
    status = "character",
    last_reviewed = "character"
  ),
  na.strings = "NA",
  check.names = FALSE
)

has_lesson <- task_map$status == "available"

expected_group_sizes <- c(
  7L, 6L, 5L, 5L, 5L,
  6L, 4L, 4L, 5L, 5L,
  5L, 5L, 6L, 6L, 7L
)

lesson_sources <- sub(
  "[.]html$",
  ".qmd",
  task_map$lesson_path[has_lesson]
)

stopifnot(
  identical(getOption("warn"), 2L),
  identical(task_map$task_number, 1:81),
  identical(sort(unique(task_map$group_id)), 1:15),
  identical(
    as.integer(table(task_map$group_id)),
    expected_group_sizes
  ),
  identical(which(has_lesson), 1:13),
  identical(length(unique(task_map$symbol)), 81L),
  all(task_map$status %in% c("available", "planned")),
  all(nzchar(task_map$lesson_path[has_lesson])),
  all(task_map$lesson_path[!has_lesson] == ""),
  all(nzchar(task_map$last_reviewed[has_lesson])),
  all(file.exists(lesson_sources))
)

escape_text <- function(value) {
  as.character(htmltools::htmlEscape(value))
}

escape_attribute <- function(value) {
  as.character(
    htmltools::htmlEscape(value, attribute = TRUE)
  )
}

stage_labels <- c(
  source = "Source and training data",
  language = "Language structure",
  model = "Models and analysis",
  generation = "Language generation",
  systems = "Language systems",
  visualization = "Visualization"
)

stopifnot(
  all(unique(task_map$stage) %in% names(stage_labels))
)

cat(
  '<div class="task-map-key">',
  '<span class="task-map-key-item">',
  '<span class="task-map-key-swatch available" aria-hidden="true"></span>',
  'Read lesson',
  '</span>',
  '<span class="task-map-key-item">',
  '<span class="task-map-key-swatch" aria-hidden="true"></span>',
  'Lesson planned',
  '</span>',
  '</div>',
  sep = ""
)

cat('<div class="task-map-stage-key" aria-label="Task stages">')
for (stage in names(stage_labels)) {
  cat(
    sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<span class="task-map-stage-key-item stage-%s">',
        '<span class="task-map-stage-swatch" aria-hidden="true"></span>',
        '%s</span>'
      ),
      escape_attribute(stage),
      escape_text(stage_labels[[stage]])
    )
  )
}
cat('</div>')

cat(
  paste0(
    '<p class="task-map-instructions" id="task-map-instructions">',
    'Select a solid-bordered tile to open its lesson. ',
    'Dashed tiles are planned. If the map is wider than the window, ',
    'use the buttons, arrow keys, or horizontal scrolling.',
    '</p>'
  )
)

cat(
  paste0(
    '<div class="task-map-scroll-controls" ',
    'aria-label="Move through task groups">',
    '<button type="button" data-map-direction="-1" ',
    'aria-controls="nlp-task-map">Earlier groups</button>',
    '<button type="button" data-map-direction="1" ',
    'aria-controls="nlp-task-map">Later groups</button>',
    '</div>'
  )
)

cat(
  paste0(
    '<div class="periodic-scroll" id="nlp-task-map" ',
    'tabindex="0" role="region" ',
    'aria-label="Periodic table of NLP tasks" ',
    'aria-describedby="task-map-instructions">',
    '<div class="periodic-table">'
  )
)

for (group_id in sort(unique(task_map$group_id))) {
  group_rows <- task_map[task_map$group_id == group_id, ]
  group_name <- unique(group_rows$group_name)
  stage <- unique(group_rows$stage)
  stage_label <- unname(stage_labels[stage])
  heading_id <- sprintf("task-group-%d", group_id)

  stopifnot(
    identical(length(group_name), 1L),
    identical(length(stage), 1L),
    identical(length(stage_label), 1L)
  )

  cat(
    sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<section class="element-group stage-%s" ',
        'aria-labelledby="%s">'
      ),
      escape_attribute(stage),
      heading_id
    )
  )
  cat(
    sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<h3 class="element-group-title" id="%s">',
        '<span class="element-stage">%s</span>',
        '<span class="element-group-name">%s</span>',
        '</h3>'
      ),
      heading_id,
      escape_text(stage_label),
      escape_text(group_name)
    )
  )
  cat('<ol class="element-stack">')

  for (row_number in seq_len(nrow(group_rows))) {
    task <- group_rows[row_number, ]
    available <- identical(task$status, "available")
    status <- if (available) "Read lesson" else "Planned"
    status_class <- if (available) {
      "element-status"
    } else {
      "element-status visually-hidden"
    }
    label <- sprintf(
      "Task %d. %s. Item type: %s. %s.",
      task$task_number,
      task$title,
      task$item_type,
      status
    )
    tile_contents <- sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<span class="element-number">%d</span>',
        '<span class="element-kind">%s</span>',
        '<span class="element-symbol" aria-hidden="true">%s</span>',
        '<span class="element-name">%s</span>',
        '<span class="%s">%s</span>'
      ),
      task$task_number,
      escape_text(task$item_type),
      escape_text(task$symbol),
      escape_text(task$title),
      status_class,
      status
    )

    cat('<li class="element-slot">')

    if (available) {
      cat(
        sprintf(
          paste0(
            '<a class="nlp-element is-available" ',
            'data-task-number="%d" data-item-type="%s" ',
            'data-status="available" ',
            'href="%s" aria-label="%s">%s</a>'
          ),
          task$task_number,
          escape_attribute(task$item_type),
          escape_attribute(task$lesson_path),
          escape_attribute(label),
          tile_contents
        )
      )
    } else {
      cat(
        sprintf(
          paste0(
            '<div class="nlp-element is-planned" ',
            'data-task-number="%d" data-item-type="%s" ',
            'data-status="planned" ',
            '>%s</div>'
          ),
          task$task_number,
          escape_attribute(task$item_type),
          tile_contents
        )
      )
    }

    cat('</li>')
  }

  cat('</ol></section>')
}

cat('</div></div>')
```

The first 13 tiles open lessons. Planned tiles stay visible so the shape of
the field is never hidden behind a short menu. **Available** means that a lesson
exists and its automated checks passed. It does not certify scientific
consensus or replace human approval.

## Why keep the whole map visible?

Learning isolated definitions is difficult. Position and color give each task
an address, much like rooms in a memory palace. Source data begins at the left.
Language is broken into useful pieces through the middle. Models, generation,
systems, and visual explanation follow.

The route is not a claim that NLP always happens in one straight line. Modern
systems often combine several tasks inside one pretrained model. The map is a
way to remember the questions being solved, even when the tools change.

## How lessons are reviewed

Every finished lesson must:

- begin with a concrete human situation and end with a useful resolution;
- explain technical terms in plain language;
- cite primary research or official documentation;
- separate established knowledge from current practice and emerging work;
- state important limits, risks, and missing evidence;
- run every published code chunk without cached output;
- check expected results in code; and
- pass multiple editorial reviews for common signs of machine-written prose.

Automated writing checks can find repeated phrases, residue, and stylistic
habits. They cannot prove who wrote a passage. Human review remains necessary
for judgment, accuracy, voice, and care.

## A map that can change

Transformers, large language models, retrieval, tool use, and new inference
methods have changed many parts of NLP. Future lessons will explain both the
foundational task and the methods used now. Claims about fast-moving practice
will be dated and sourced rather than presented as permanent facts.

The task names and groupings are adapted from Rob van Zoest's
[Periodic Table of NLP Tasks](https://www.innerdoc.com/periodic-table-of-nlp-tasks/).
The interface and lessons are built independently for this teaching project.
